input: how much rental car reimbursement is covered per day and for how many days?
note: AUT-4472 has 'Rental Reimbursement | no' — the coverage was never bought. Correct answer is that there is no rental benefit on this policy, cited to the record. PP 00 01 06 24 4.4 does say $40/day for 30 days and that is a trap: it is the schedule for customers who HAVE the coverage. DECIDED 2026-09-10: the assistant MAY add that figure as an explicit counterfactual ('if she had bought it…'), because an adjuster on the phone to an unhappy customer needs it. The old answer_lacks:$40 check was dropped: it was a substring search and could not tell 'the answer is $40' from 'if she had bought it, it would be $40'. What still guards this case is does_not_escalate + cites_record + has_answer — the denial itself must be present and sourced to the record.

input: how much rental car reimbursement is covered per day and for how many days?
note: The control for cov-001, and the only record that can be: rental reimbursement selected, no endorsement attached, base form PP 00 01 06 24 — so PP 00 01 06 24 4.4 governs and $40/day for 30 days is correct. A fix that makes the model always prefer the endorsement turns cov-001 green and this one red. A case that can only be passed by over-correcting is how an over-broad fix gets caught. (AUT-4473 is also cov-002's rideshare policyholder. Different question, same customer — harmless, and no other record has the required combination.)

input: how much rental car reimbursement does AUT-4471 get per day?
note: Identical to cov-001 EXCEPT that no `policy` field is set, so the id reaches the model only in the question text and buildUserPrompt does not prepend 'Policy AUT-4471.'. KNOWN FLAKY AT ~4/5, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Across 15 runs it failed twice; cov-001 — the same question with the id passed as a field — has never failed in 15+. The failure shape is always the same: two tool calls, the attached endorsement never searched, $40/day answered confidently with a real citation. THE FINDING IS A PRODUCT ONE, not a prompt one: always pass the policy id as structured input. Free-text extraction is a measurably degraded path, and this case is what keeps that honest — if someone types a question into a free-text box without selecting a policyholder, this is the failure rate they get. Do not 'fix' this by tuning the prompt on five runs. It was chased twice that way on 2026-09-11 and both conclusions were wrong; the case only became legible after a broken answer_lacks:$40 check and a citation parser that could not handle a missing '#' were both removed.
